FRENCH — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #11
====

GRADE: Grade 8
SUBJECT: FRENCH
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KJSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When practising Interactive Speaking, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Interactive Speaking.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Interactive Speaking.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Interactive Speaking.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Interactive Speaking.

2. When practising Listening for information, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Listening for information.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Listening for information.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Listening for information.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening for information.

3. When practising Active Listening, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Active Listening.

   D. Copy random text without understanding Active Listening.

   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Interactive Speaking Turn taking Vocabulary Engagement Questioning.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Interactive Speaking Turn taking Vocabulary Engagement Questioning.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Interactive Speaking Turn taking Vocabulary Engagement Questioning.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Interactive Speaking Turn taking Vocabulary Engagement Questioning.

   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Interactive speaking Vocabulary Turn taking Intonation Nonverbal communication.

10. The French word for “book” is: (1 mark)
   A. chaise
   B. livre
   C. fenêtre
   D. porte

11. “Bonjour” is used to say: (1 mark)
   A. Excuse me
   B. Good morning / hello
   C. Good night only
   D. Thank you

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
12. In three clear sentences, explain Reading for fluency and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

13. In three clear sentences, explain Reading for understanding and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

MARKING SCHEME
====

1. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Interactive Speaking.

2. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening for information.

3. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Active Listening.

4. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Interactive speaking Turn taking Nonverbal communication Intonation Questioning.

5. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Interactive listening 1.3 Active listening 1.4 Listening for information.

6. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Interactive Speaking Turn taking Vocabulary Engagement Questioning.

7. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Interactive speaking Vocabulary Turn taking Intonation Nonverbal communication.

8. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Oral Expression.

9. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening for understanding Identifying key points Vocabulary Attention.

10. B — livre

11. B — Good morning / hello

Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Reading for fluency; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
